description: R3-05 independent-review FP (r9-kernel-econ-guard, reviewer claude-opus-5-5-high): two legitimate, sequential, same-amount deposits to the attacker's own wallet resource (`POST /v1/wallets/<walletId>/deposit`), each response echoing the wallet object's top-level `id`, bracketed by own-tenant balance readbacks whose delta exactly equals the sum of both deposits. The wallet/account resource id is NOT an economic entity (order/payment/invoice) id, so the deposits must not be collapsed into one entity (max-per-entity dedup would under-count authorizedDeposits by half) and must not satisfy duplicate-entity credit multiplicity. Balance is fully conserved; balance_minting must fail closed. The authored branch keyed both deposits by the wallet id (top-level response `id` / dynamic path segment) and confirmed it. Coverage note: the verdict runs through own-org-terminal-guard/v8-oracle-hydrate (hydrateBalanceMintingOperands) and exec-verify's composite host-origin inspection; the verify-rpc cap:* persona auto-lift path is exercised live by tests/r9-kernel-econ-guard.test.ts test 2 (no RPC transport in the static corpus runner).

canonicalLabel.title: Sequential own-wallet deposits misread as balance minting
canonicalLabel.impact: Two authorized deposits to the same wallet conserve balance exactly; collapsing them by wallet resource id under-counts authorized deposits and fabricates a conservation break.

composite.claimedDelta: Two sequential deposits to the same wallet resource minted balance beyond the authorized deposit amount.
